title: A new bill could change how the US builds energy infrastructure
abstract: A sweeping bit of legislation designed to cut red tape could speed up the buildout of energy infrastructure in the US. With the dust barely settled on this week’s momentous midterms, the Senate is set to vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on November 9. It’s a plan that could finally start an overhaul of the slow, complicated process for getting energy projects approved, as part of something called permitting reform. People on both sides of the political aisle have been pushing for this type of change for some years. The key question is whether this will cut greenhouse-gas emissions from the US energy sector or push them higher still. The federal permitting system is designed to protect the environment against industrial pollution from large projects like power plants, transmission lines, and natural-gas pipelines. Today, permitting is governed by a range of laws, including the National Environmental Policy Act and the Clean Water Act. And if there’s one thing you might know about the current state of permitting in the US it’s that it’s slow and incredibly complicated. So in its 417 pages, BAAJA attempts to tighten things up. The bill has provisions that narrow the sorts of projects that need to apply for federal permits and others that enact deadlines in hopes of speeding up a process that today can take years. (There are also specific provisions about transmission planning, mining, and the rest of the kitchen sink; this thing is dense .) One thing to know about this bill is that it’s largely technology neutral: It opens the doors for the buildout of projects involving both fossil fuels and renewables. So there’s a weird mishmash of legislators and outside groups supporting it. The bill’s four sponsors in the Senate are two Republicans and two Democrats. The White House has backed this permitting reform bill, with its Council of Economic Advisors finding that it would reduce review times and have economic benefits like boosting GDP. Clean energy groups like the American Clean Power Association have largely come out in favor of the bill too, with the group’s analysis finding that it could unlock 350 gigawatts of new clean energy for the grid. Some environmental groups, however, oppose the bill, or parts of it. An assessment from the Natural Resources Defense Council says the parts about transmission could have substantial benefits for the grid, but the narrowing of environmental reviews could be damaging for public and private lands. Many in the climate world have long been calling for permitting reform, arguing that renewables stand to benefit more than fossil fuels. The thinking is that solar and wind power are some of the cheapest sources available today, so if we unlock the ability to build more energy, they are likely to win out economically. A few early analyses have tried to quantify just what BAAJA would mean for emissions in the US. One, from the think tank Rhodium Group, found that in the best-case scenario, the bill would cut economy-wide emissions by 4%, reduce annual energy bills by $78 per household, and add 200 gigawatts of new clean energy by 2040. In the worst case, emissions would stay about the same. Another report , from the nonprofit research group Resources for the Future, found that the bill could cut power-sector emissions 6% by 2041 and save more than $350 billion on system costs by midcentury. title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
abstract: Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position. Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against the Republican incumbent, Greg Abbott. At the state level, Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. Talarico and Hinojosa made data centers a central issue, discussing them constantly on the campaign trail. Even before the polls closed, insiders in the data center industry noticed that the times were changing. At the industry’s DCD conference in Ashburn, Virginia, on Tuesday, panelists lamented that Texas had been the easiest place to build for years—until September. That’s when Abbott, perhaps seeing the increasingly bipartisan distaste for these facilities , began changing course himself. Developers said the governor’s office had stopped responding to their emails. On September 21, Abbott directed a key state regulator to halt data center permits. Many panelists at the conference were expecting this to mean that existing projects might be slowed and new ones could be halted altogether. The governor-elect indeed seems eager to do that. Hinojosa supported tax breaks for data centers in 2023 as a way to boost construction jobs, but during her campaign she began pushing for a full-fledged moratorium. That would be a problem for the hyperscalers of Big Tech, which have ambitious plans for AI training facilities in the state. The scale of projects already underway in Texas is massive. The Stargate Frontier data center in Shackelford County is projected to serve 1,820 megawatts—about as much as the nation’s largest data center, SpaceX’s Colossus 2 in Tennessee, and more than twice as much as the largest data center currently operating in Texas. Nexus Hubbard, also under construction and intended mostly to serve Anthropic, has a planned size of 6,400 megawatts and is the second-largest data center being built in the US, behind only Meta’s Hyperion project in Louisiana. The potential for Democrats to order delays to these projects or moratoriums on new ones adds to growing anxiety that the AI buildout could stall. Banks and lenders are already getting pickier about the projects they back. And given the extent to which the data center buildout is underpinning growth in the economy right now, those forces combined could have ripple effects. Voters around the country, though, were unambiguous in the midterms, sending a similar message on everything from state ballot questions to national offices. Voters supported efforts to protect ratepayers from increases in their electricity bills caused by data centers, and they favored some larger bans on new data centers altogether. If we needed any more convincing that Big Tech has fumbled its effort to sell voters on the idea that AI-powered abundance will make health care better, goods cheaper, and scientific breakthroughs more common, this was it. A key question is whether the Texas counties with the largest data center presence were part of the reason these Democrats got elected, or if the anti-data-center vote came from elsewhere. It’s complicated: The counties where much of the data center buildout is happening are around Dallas. Dallas County and others closest to it predictably went blue, but nearby Ellis County, which leads in permitting requests for data centers, went for Greg Abbott and Ken Paxton. Cameron County, near the state’s southern border, is a hot spot for data centers and voted blue in the midterms, which was a shift. But Mitchell County and Scurry County, where a bunch of projects in west Texas are located, went red. This is a big deal, because no single office in the state decides whether a project goes ahead or is halted. Decisions often reflect an interplay between city governments, county officials, and state offices. Local officials

title: What’s next for US energy policy after the midterm elections?
abstract: I’ve been locked in to my various screens since results from midterm elections started to roll in last night. And it didn’t take long to see the beginning of the blue wave: Democrats took control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate, a dramatic swing from Donald Trump’s victory two years ago. While the results are striking, we probably won’t be seeing some of the big climate and energy policy shifts that have come in recent years as Congress and the presidency have changed hands. Instead, we’re entering a period of divided government, with a Congress that will likely do battle with Trump’s White House over the next two years. But even if the federal government isn’t likely to pass laws that overhaul energy and climate policy, the midterm results could be a big deal for energy, especially at the state and local level. Let’s step back for just a moment to put these results in context. Readers might remember huge laws affecting climate and energy that were passed in just the last four years. The 2022 Inflation Reduction Act included massive support for clean energy, including tax credits and government grants and loans. Then the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act essentially slashed much of the support and financial incentives in the IRA from two years before. What those two laws had in common was a period when the government was entirely united, with the Senate, House of Representatives, and presidency all controlled by the same party—the Democrats in the first case and the Republicans in the second. Now Democrats have captured a majority in both the Senate and the House. But Donald Trump is still in the White House. And crucially, neither chamber is anywhere close to a two-thirds Democratic majority. That’s the ratio that would be needed to override a presidential veto. So even if Congress puts together new legislation to boost climate measures and clean energy, Trump will need to sign it—and that dramatically narrows the scope of what might happen legislatively between now and the next election. There could be some bipartisan compromises. One interesting bit of legislation to watch immediately after the election is what happens with permitting reform. In late September, a bipartisan group of senators put forward a bill that would overhaul how new energy projects are reviewed and approved in the US. The law aims to cut red tape and speed up the permitting process. The Senate is set to vote on that package, called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, on November 9, before the new Congress takes control in January. The White House has supported the bill, and it could pass the Senate if just a handful of Democrats join the Republican majority. But now, we might see Democrats wait until next year to try to renegotiate a deal, though anything would still need to pass muster with Trump. With Democratic control of Congress, we’ll likely see much more scrutiny of Trump and agencies controlled by his appointees. Democratic leaders have already signaled plans to go after leaders like EPA commissioner Lee Zeldin over cuts to staff and investments. Democrats will have the power to subpoena cabinet members and open investigations. Looking beyond the national results, a major trend to watch moving forward will be local action. Democrats swept local control of Pennsylvania, and officials there have signaled plans to support renewable energy and efforts to cut greenhouse-gas emissions. Democrats also took control of the Georgia Public Service Commission for the first time in 30 years. The group regulates electric utilities, essentially controlling much of the grid’s buildout. Among the broadest effects of these election results, though, will be for the data center industry. According to tracking from Ballotpedia, there were 41 local ballot questions related to data centers. And overwhelmingly, voters chose to restrict their development. title: The Download: blended meat, restored sight, and the agentic web
abstract: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. These startups hope “blended” food will cut our appetite for red meat In the fall of 2025, Jeff Dodge served hungry students steaming marinara sauce and meatballs. The students loved them: 92% of those who tried them wanted them on the menu. Few could guess that mushrooms had been mixed into the meat. Dodge was testing a new product called 50/Cut from the company Joyn. The blend of seemingly simple ingredients—available as meatballs, burgers, and ground meat—could help solve one of the biggest challenges of the climate crisis: getting people to eat less meat, particularly beef. Joyn is among a wave of startups creating “blended meat,” which combines plant proteins with the real deal. The logic: The best meat replacement is … better meat. Get a taste of the startups betting on greener beef . —Meghan McCarron This implant can restore sight for patients with macular degeneration More than 5 million people have an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) called geographic atrophy, in which retinal cells die off. Until now, no treatment could restore their vision. A system called PRIMA changes that. It combines a retinal implant with camera-equipped eyeglasses to improve sight in patients who develop a blind spot in the middle of their vision. After training sessions, more than 80% of recipients could read, do crosswords, and use their phones. Find out how the sight-restoring implant works . —Linda Marsa MIT Technology Review Narrated: The agentic web is here In 2001, a decade after inventing the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision: an internet navigated by autonomous software agents that address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves. At the time, the idea seemed far-fetched. But a quarter-century on, AI agents are beginning to make it a reality. They can triage your inbox, do your grocery shopping, and even access your bank accounts. This new era is being called the agentic web, and it will inevitably transform the internet. Whether the human web survives this transition is anyone’s guess . title: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
abstract: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents. DOWNLOAD THE REPORT This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically. As more enterprises begin to use agentic AI in daily workflows, they’re realizing that they must manage more than static files; they must manage moving and fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed in new forms. In short, AI security isn’t a tool problem; it’s a data visibility problem. Consequently, traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient. Securing agentic AI at scale requires understanding how data moves. Teams, therefore, need to establish data lineage in order to effectively manage governance, accountability, and trust across human, agentic, and hybrid workflows. title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
abstract: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law, hack into unauthorized servers, or release poison gas into major cities and kill us all. Until now, this work has mostly focused on trying to peer into an AI’s “brain” to understand what it is “thinking,” or training models to hew to values that we hold dear. Claude, for instance, has its constitution —a sort of moral code. The trouble is, these techniques don’t seem to work particularly well: Models have been shown to deliberately underperform on tests, hide their intentions , and mislead their evaluators . Now some alignment researchers believe that reverse game theory, also known as mechanism design, might get better results. Where game theory tries to predict how rational actors will behave when given a particular set of rules, reverse game theory attempts to design rules that will elicit the kinds of behavior we want to encourage. An example of mechanism design in the real world might be the classic strategy for splitting a piece of cake in two: One person cuts the cake and the other gets the first choice of pieces. This incentivizes the cutter to make the pieces as even as possible. Other examples include surge pricing in ride-hailing apps, which encourages drivers to be available at busy times, and second-price auctions, where the winning bidder pays the price of the second-highest bid instead of the highest. Platforms use these auctions to sell online advertising because they encourage buyers to bid close to the maximum they are willing to pay. In AI, mechanism design starts from the premise that we may never be able to understand enough about the internal workings of frontier models to make sure they are aligned. This means we should design mechanisms that incentivize agents to behave in ways that we want, regardless of what’s actually going on under the hood. A recent preprint paper by Stephen Morris, an economist at MIT, along with colleagues from Yale and Columbia suggested some potential mechanisms that could stop agents from “sandbagging” tests (pretending to be worse than they actually are—for example, to avoid triggering safety mechanisms). Instead of being rewarded only for how well it does on a test, a model could be rewarded for how well its answers predict what a second model will say. Deliberately playing dumb becomes a losing bet. “AI agents have a very good understanding of what other AI agents can achieve,” Morris says. “So it does seem like a context where this cross-checking could work more practically. The paper also suggests pitting agents against each other, creating a competitive dynamic that incentivizes them to perform their best, or pairing agents that are known to be biased in opposite directions and rewarding them depending on how closely their outputs match, thus incentivizing them to reach an optimal answer. A second approach, as envisioned by Elad Hazan, a professor of computer science at Princeton, is to design mechanisms that take inspiration from the ways human society keeps people “aligned”: social norms, the justice system, the monetary incentives of free-market capitalism. “We want to align superintelligent AI,” he says. “Why don’t we first talk about humans? How do we align humans?” Hazan’s suggested mechanism involves having AI models take turns as either “solvers” that tackle problems or “auditors” that check the others’ work. “One agent acts like law enforcement; the other agent acts like the citizen,” he says. During training, the models are rewarded depending on outcomes: Solvers that get caught cheating are punished, but so are auditors that fail to catch the cheaters. title: Here’s who is falling in line for Trump’s “Super Intelligence” loyalty test
abstract: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here . At the end of September, President Trump signed an executive order that contained just one directive, ordering government agencies to rebrand what they had been calling artificial intelligence as “Super Intelligence.” That term beat out other contenders, including “Extreme Intelligence” and “Supreme Intelligence,” offered by the president in a poll on X a couple of weeks earlier. Rebrands are, of course, now a White House tradition: Trump has changed names to project US dominance of certain bodies of water (the Gulf of America and Lake America), to signal new institutional priorities (Department of War), or simply to leave his mark on storied places (see the ongoing fight over renaming the Kennedy Center). The stated reason for this name change is that today’s AI systems “amplify human ingenuity” rather than merely “imitate” intelligence, and the government’s terminology should reflect that. But if this rebrand follows the pattern of others, its effects will extend beyond government. It will turn a choice of words into a political loyalty test: Those who use the new term demonstrate allegiance to the administration, and those who don’t become marks for attacks (recall that the Trump administration barred the Associated Press from some White House press events after the news outlet did not adopt the term “Gulf of America”). But most Americans go months without ever pondering what to call the major lake between New York and Canada. AI, on the other hand, is at the center of our national conversation and a technology two-thirds of Americans report interacting with multiple times a week. It might be the boldest rebrand yet. So one month in, who’s on board? Let’s start with the government itself. The term “Super Intelligence”—or simply “SI”—now appears more often on government solicitations, like a new request by Immigration and Customs Enforcement for companies to build “SI-powered” surveillance for ICE detention facilities. The new term has been swapped in silently on most government websites. Some, including that of the National Institutes of Health, now include a banner warning visitors they might see both the new and the old terms during the transition period. There have been hiccups. A day after the rebrand order, the Pentagon announced an ambitious new initiative to study the future of warfare, called Project Meridian; it used the old terminology. A Federal Trade Commission press release last week used “superintelligence” instead of the two-word, capitalized version ordered by the president, and recent press releases from Health and Human Services show no sign of the new language. The term “AI” will likely stick around given the countless AI-related offices, initiatives, and programs that have sprung up in recent years, like the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office at the Pentagon (the executive order says it doesn’t apply to previously issued regulations or documents). As for government employees, it appears to be taking time for “SI” rather than “AI” to roll off the tongue. One researcher at a national lab I interviewed a few weeks ago used “AI” repeatedly before sheepishly acknowledging the slip-up. Even Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used “AI” in an interview on October 3. But Trump’s other rebrands suggest the goal isn’t merely to change the government’s vocabulary. It’s to change how the rest of us speak, too. In the past couple of weeks, most of President Trump’s posts on Truth Social have been endorsements for candidates in the midterms. But on October 27 he took a break from electioneering to criticize the Wall Street Journal for not using “Super Intelligence,” “the name which virtually everyone else is using, or soon will be.” He suggested that a new rule will soon go further than the executive order to outright ban “artificial intelligence” from government documents

title: AI Text Watermarking May Not Be Able to Meet the E.U.’s New Rules
abstract: The European Union now requires AI-generated text to be watermarked so that it can be identified as such. But tests on OpenAI’s new textGrain watermark, released in October and developed to comply with the new E.U. law , show that these watermarks often do not survive additional editing of the text or when it’s under 150 words. With no clear legal benchmark for how well watermarks should work, it’s uncertain whether textGrain will meet Europe’s transparency rules, which could cost the company significantly and make it difficult to detect AI-generated text as models grow more sophisticated. AI models calculate the probabilities of different possible next “tokens” (the next word or word fragment it generates) based on the text already written, then select one and repeat that process until the response is complete. After the prompt “today the weather is…,” for example, says Xiang Li , coauthor of the textGrain technical report and a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Pennsylvania, the model might weigh “warm” or “cool” as possible next words. A watermark uses a secret key to generate pseudorandom values—numbers produced by a mathematical process that influence which token the model suggests. This creates a statistical pattern in the text that a detector with the same secret key can look for, Li says. What makes textGrain different from other watermarks is that it uses entropy, a measure of how unpredictable a model’s word choices are, as a resource that can be budgeted when embedding a watermark. Developers specify how much entropy or unpredictability they want to allow, and textGrain adjusts to that target. This gives developers more control over the balance between embedding a detectable signal and preserving variation in the model’s output, Li says. “We can think of entropy as a resource, a kind of money.… In our approach, we can accurately determine how much of that resource we want to consume.” Limits of AI Watermark Detection The watermark is invisible to readers. But a positive result does not show how much a person contributed to a passage, and a negative result does not prove that a text was human-written. OpenAI’s false-positive rate is 1 percent, meaning the detector is designed to wrongly flag about one in 100 unwatermarked passages. In tests on psychology questions from the ELI5 database , which gathers questions and answers from the r/explainlikeimfive subreddit, the model detected watermarks in about 80 percent of 200-token text ( approximately 150 words ) compared to 95 percent of 400-token text (approximately 300 words). Li says this is a “basic limitation” of text-watermarking technologies and would be complicated to solve. Short passages may not contain enough watermark evidence for reliable detection, even with additional computation, he adds, while longer passages generally provide more. Editing also weakens the signal. In an evaluation of 400-token passages, replacing just 10 percent of words with synonyms reduced detection from 92 percent to 66 percent; replacing up to 25 percent cut the detection rate to 17 percent, according to OpenAI. Because the watermark depends on preceding tokens, changing one word can disrupt the signal at several positions, Li says. OpenAI says watermarking alone is not enough to determine whether content is AI-generated. TextGrain will “complement” other provenance tools, such as content credentials in the metadata and SynthID watermarks developed by Google DeepMind for images and audio outputs. OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment. E.U. AI Act Transparency Obligations The transparency obligations in Article 50 of the E.U. AI Act went into effect on 2 August. The law requires providers of systems generating synthetic audio, images, video, or text to mark outputs in a machine-readable format so they can be detected as artificially generated or manipulated. title: How a Kenyan Startup Is Rethinking AI for Small Businesses
abstract: The first time Mutembei Kariuki thought about how AI models could work in Kenya, his home country, was in 2019. He was attending a conference at the University of Tokyo on the future of AI, and kept hearing about how this technology was going to transform the world. “But nobody mentioned Africa at all,” he says. Even then—before AI giants like OpenAI and Anthropic had launched their chatbots to the public—Kariuki could see significant obstacles to AI adoption in Africa. Internet access was slow and unequal, computing resources for training models were scarce, and there was little high-quality, structured training data. Most people, meanwhile, reached the internet through outdated, low-memory cellphones rather than computers or high-end phones. Together with cofounders Jude Mwenda and Stephanie Njerenga , Kariuki created Fastagger , a startup that builds AI models that can run offline and on low-power cellphones. Its first big product, Auni, is a business-intelligence assistant that launched in 2024; it got a big push when it was integrated into the business app of M-Pesa , Kenya’s largest mobile money service. Since then, about 6,000 businesses have signed up. Auni helps small and medium businesses like barbershops, restaurants, and small manufacturers analyze their transaction data and gives them marketing recommendations. Peter Chege, owner of a salon and barbershop in Nairobi, started using Auni last year. Before that, he recorded all his sales on paper. “We were not able to translate that information into a graph,” he says. Now, the app helps him identify his busiest days and hours, as well as his loyal customers. If a regular customer stops coming, for example, he can send a personalized message encouraging them to return. Fastagger is part of an emerging effort to build AI around the technological realities of users in developing economies, rather than adapting products designed for wealthier markets. In Fastagger’s case, that meant finding a way to make their models work despite inexpensive phones, unreliable internet connections, and business records that may consist of little more than mobile-money transactions. Designing AI for Kenya’s Small Businesses Before developing Auni, Kariuki and his cofounders started by tackling the problem of data availability for AI training. They asked themselves: “How do we get Africa to catch up fast? How do we create training data fast enough, and then how do we actually get it into people’s hands fast enough?” Mutembei Kariuki cofounded Fastagger to develop AI systems that can run offline and on basic phones. Afrikanna Production/Microsoft They decided to focus on mobile phones, and specifically on mobile money apps. With more than 80 percent of Kenya’s adults using them, they offer a rich source of data. One of Fastagger’s first steps was to adapt an open-source optical character recognition (OCR) model to read financial statements produced by mobile money apps. Existing models struggled with the low quality of the PDFs, which had unfamiliar formatting and sometimes contained stamps and errors. And because Fastagger’s prospective users often had unreliable internet connections, they made sure that key steps, like organizing the extracted data into tables, could run on-device. Once they had a model that could process these documents, they began exploring how that structured financial data could help businesses. They spent entire days watching small-business owners work and interact with their customers. One challenge quickly became clear: Owners had little time or resources to think beyond day-to-day operations. “They are standing up the whole day cutting hair,” Kariuki says of salon owners, who are now among Auni’s main users. “You have to think about that dynamic of the user journey, and how they live, and what will be going on in the background.” The Fastagger app helps salon owner Peter Chege better manage his time and keep track of loyal customers. abstract: KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, Fla.—Blue Origin announced two significant upgrades to its New Glenn rocket on Thursday, reducing the cost of manufacturing the vehicle and expanding its capacity for payload delivery to geostationary orbit and the Moon. With these upgrades, the company aims to eventually position New Glenn to launch more than 1,000 times a year. "There has never been higher demand for launch, ever," Dave Limp, chief executive officer of Blue Origin, said during the UP.Summit conference at the Shuttle Landing Facility in Florida. title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
abstract: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations. One connection, works every time, needs no retries There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a "*" in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored. Passwordless accounts are commonly used for accounts that use certificate-based authentication. This setting is common for certain types of accounts. Read full article Comments

title: NASA unveils mysterious X-70 experimental aircraft using AI-generated image
abstract: NASA has announced a new experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, that will supposedly feature reconfigurable flight-control technology and a modular design for swapping in different payloads. But much remains unknown about the aircraft’s design and development timeline, even as NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said the X-plane could take flight within two years. The mystery surrounding NASA’s newest X-plane was exemplified by the agency’s press release, including an apparently AI-generated image of the X-70, showing a dark silhouette vaguely resembling a military fighter jet obscured by smoke. The news was announced by Isaacman during the UP.Summit held at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on November 4. “The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” Isaacman said. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next.” Read full article Comments

abstract: Color us nostalgic. Sony has brought back the MDR-3-series headphones that debuted in 1979 alongside the Walkman TPS-L2 cassette player. In this marketing image Sony shared, you can see the Walkman TPS-L2. Credit: Sony Originally called the "MDR-3L2," the first Walkman headphones were known for their sleek, adjustable gray plastic headband, which extended via metal sliders and ended in signature orange, circular ear cushions. The lightweight, on-ear headphones are a contrast to the bulky headsets that are popular these days, which use wide, cushioned headbands for long-term comfort and large earcups that can support big drivers and are often heavily padded for noise isolation. title: Google: Schools can keep search while skipping Gemini, but AI search is non-negotiable
abstract: Google faced the ire of educators and parents earlier this week when it announced a new AI policy for K–12 schools . Google said that it developed its new approach to give schools more control, but early reporting also suggested Google would block search access for schools that didn't want to use AI. Google didn't see the backlash coming, but now that it's here, the search giant is clarifying what exactly its new policy means and what's changing. The gist of the new policy, according to Google's blog post, is that schools using Google apps will have to opt into its AI products going forward. Since the company considers search part of its AI portfolio (Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search), schools have to specifically turn that on for logged-in student accounts. When Google revealed its new policy, the company's VP for education spoke exclusively to The New York Times , which interpreted the situation as Google will "turn off search" if schools reject AI. This has a nefarious vibe, but it's probably not the most accurate way to describe how Google's educational AI system will operate. Google's approach may not be entirely altruistic, but it technically offers schools more choice and control than they have now. Instead of Google turning off search, it will let schools make that decision based on their internal AI policies. Read full article Comments

title: Lawsuit: Man introduced his wife to ChatGPT. She used it to plan his murder.
abstract: ChatGPT allegedly helped a North Carolina woman, Cheryl Gates, craft a “personalized plan” to poison her husband, James, after fueling her delusions that he planned to divorce her and leave her with nothing. A grand jury indicted Cheryl Gates on charges of attempted first-degree murder and food contamination in October. About a week prior, the accusations that ChatGPT was a co-conspirator in the attempted murder came in a lawsuit filed in San Francisco County Superior Court that was made public this week. In it, James Gates alleged that OpenAI and Sam Altman failed to employ technical safeguards to shut down Cheryl’s chats even after her queries became “obviously suspicious” and sought advice on how to execute and conceal a homicide. At first, Cheryl told ChatGPT that she was researching poisoning out of fear that her husband might possibly try to kill her—framing her queries as “self-protection.” Coming to the rescue, ChatGPT did not terminate the conversation. Instead, it helped her “with specific instructions for the preparation, dosage, and administration of Oleander, including whether anti-nausea medicine would accelerate or inhibit death, whether it would show on an autopsy report, and whether it could be injected into a vein or muscle instead of being ingested in tea and have the same lethal effect,” the lawsuit said. title: BMW bumps battery for the better: The 2027 i7 60 xDrive, driven
abstract: BMW provided flights from Washington, DC, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the 2027 i7 as well as the 2027 iX5 and X5. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. When BMW debuted the new 7 Series in 2022, it set a new standard for large luxury sedans, increasingly irrelevant though that class is. Rather than siloing off an electric alternative like Mercedes, with its EQS alongside the normal S-Class, BMW simply made the powertrain an option. Stick with a V8 if you want, or consider the rather good electric version instead—only subtle differences like the badging and lack of exhaust pipes give the game away. Since then, BMW has brought out a string of even newer electric vehicles for the 5 and 3 Series (plus their SUV counterparts). It has switched from battery packs made of prismatic cells to more energy-dense arrangements of cylindrical cells. The motors are still electrically excited synchronous ones, but now the drive units feature silicon carbide inverters and more compact packaging. This sixth-generation electric powertrain was designed for the clean-sheet Neue Klasse family, which also threw out the legacy cruft of dozens and dozens of discrete single-function electronic control units for a handful of powerful domain controllers. These computers take over those functions but with much faster processing power—and therefore more capabilities in terms of chassis control or powertrain efficiency—as well as the ability to be more easily updated. title: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets
abstract: With a huge and still-growing catalog of exoplanets, researchers are eager to take the next steps: trying to infer what conditions are like on them, either by imaging them directly or by capturing the light that has passed through their atmosphere. Both are substantial challenges, given the presence of stars that are far, far brighter than light that has come to us via the planet. While telescopes can be fitted with devices called coronagraphs that block out much of a star's light, there are limits to their effectiveness, caused by noise from subtle variations in the telescope's configuration and pointing between observations. Now, researchers have developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the telescope in a way that allows us to better model these differences, producing low-noise imaging of exoplanets. Point spreads Central to this work is the concept of a point spread function. If you use a telescope to image a single point of light, it will not appear that way in the actual image. Instead, it will be slightly blurry and spread out, due to imperfections in the telescope hardware and the limits of our ability to keep it pointed accurately through the time it takes to image something. The mathematical description of how a telescope distorts a point of light is called its point spread function. Read full article Comments

title: Kalshi court losses pile up as judges refuse to block state gambling laws
abstract: Kalshi is having a bad week in the federal court system. Two circuit appeals courts rejected the prediction market's latest attempts to block state gambling laws in Connecticut, New York, and Nevada. Kalshi is separately facing a new lawsuit filed by the Arkansas attorney general. In all cases involving Kalshi and state governments around the US, the main issue is whether state gambling laws apply to prediction markets despite Kalshi's claim that its platform offers "swaps" that can only be regulated by the US Commodity Futures Exchange (CFTC). The Trump administration is on Kalshi's side, with Donald Trump Jr. serving as an advisor to Kalshi in exchange for a generous equity deal . "Kalshi insists that its products are not gambling," but "Arkansas law is concerned with substance, not semantics," Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin said yesterday when announcing his lawsuit against Kalshi. Kalshi's prediction market lets customers "wager money on the outcome of just about anything" despite the fact that "gambling on an unregulated platform is squarely prohibited by Arkansas law," he said. title: MAHA lost bigly in the midterms—is it at death's door?
abstract: As Democrats blew away their Republican rivals in an unprecedented midterm sweep Tuesday, the Make America Health Again movement also got bowled over, raising questions about the fate of the motley movement. MAHA—which has centered around anti-vaccine activist and current Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.—saw many of its favored candidates and allies lose, while vocal adversaries of Kennedy won. And the coalition was splintering under stress even before the voting started; in recent months, supporters have accused Kennedy and the Trump administration of inaction and betrayals in their two years in power. Now hobbled in Washington, shedding supporters, and showing little to no influence in voting booths, is MAHA on its deathbed? Or will it be reborn—possibly into a new group? Could it be assimilated into a blue platform—after sloughing off the more repulsive, conspiratorial aspects of Kennedy's ideology? These are the questions circling in the aftermath of Tuesday's bloodbath. Read full article Comments

title: Gamers go to ridiculous lengths to "improve" GTA VI with Nvidia's DLSS 5
abstract: While the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI won't be available on PC this month, some gamers are making ridiculous preparations to use their PC graphics cards to apply Nvidia's DLSS 5 technology to the console exclusive. On an explicitly unmoderated GTAVI subreddit, user RevolutionaryBus8208 lays out a proposed setup, which runs a PlayStation 5 through a 4K capture card to a PC. From there, the video signal is run through Veyra , an open source tool that can apply DLSS 5's AI-powered "neural rendering" to video content. The result—which also uses DLSS frame generation to increase the 30 fps source to a 90 fps output—is then piped back to a 4K TV, theoretically adding some of the benefits of a beefy PC graphics card to a console-exclusive game. To demonstrate the potential of this setup, RevolutionaryBus8208 used Veyra to upscale the Grand Theft Auto VI Extended Look trailer posted in August. The resulting DLSS-ified version looks a bit better in places, with sharper background elements, subtler shadows, and more believable light scattering on some surfaces. But it also seems a bit washed out compared to the original video's deeper blacks and arguably suffers from an unnaturally smooth "soap opera effect" in some scenes. Read full article Comments

That advantage has disappeared, clearing the path for more climate and clean energy legislation, according to analysts and advocates. Democrats swept the vast majority of competitive races at the state level, flipping control of governors’ offices from Republicans in Georgia, Iowa, Ohio, Nevada, and Texas. title: Motorola's new Signature 27 has it all if you can stomach the $1,600 price tag
abstract: Motorola is patching a hole in its US lineup with a non-folding flagship phone, but the pricing puts this device dangerously close to the company's expensive tablet-style foldable . The long-rumored Motorola Signature 27 is real, featuring top-of-the-line specs, a super-bright OLED screen, and a ton of cameras. But all this high-end hardware won't come cheap in the age of AI. Motorola's new flagship smartphone will run a whopping $1,600 when it arrives later this month. The Signature 27 is a new take on flagship smartphones from Motorola, leaving behind the middling legacy of the Edge series. However, you'll still immediately clock this as a Motorola device due to its distinctive use of materials and Pantone colors. The phone is metal, ceramic, and glass, but the backs are textured polycarbonate. The device comes in Coal Smoke (black) or Capulet Olive (green) colors. The former has a "tactical weave" finish inspired by automotive design, and the latter is "textile-inspired." This device will include the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, the most powerful mobile chip Qualcomm offers right now. While some smartphones have flirted with 16GB of memory, that's less common these days. The Signature 27 will have 12GB like Samsung's base model flagships. However, there's not going to be an upgrade option for more. You will, however, get a generous 512GB of storage. Read full article Comments

title: Agility Robotics' Nasdaq debut invites scrutiny of humanoid robot market
abstract: Humanoid robots remain unproven at scale and have not yet achieved widespread commercialization, compared with industrial robots that have decades of proven track records in warehouses and factories. That frank acknowledgment is among the risks outlined in a securities filing by Agility Robotics—the first dedicated developer of humanoid robots to become a publicly traded company in the United States. The robotics company, headquartered in Salem, Oregon, previously became the first to achieve full-time commercial deployment of humanoid robots at a customer warehouse in 2024. Now, Agility’s public listing on the Nasdaq stock exchange as of November 5 has come with financial disclosures detailing how the company plans to build a business around renting out or selling humanoid robots to perform manual labor. “When we are doing robots as a service, it is much lower risk for customers to use it because they are getting a return on investment on day one,” Jonathan Hurst , co-founder and chief robot officer at Agility Robotics, told Ars. "Because they're paying a rate that is comparable to the human labor rate, and that makes the economics pretty straightforward.” Read full article Comments

title: 2026 iPad mini review: Maximizing the mini
abstract: The iPad mini has long felt like a niche product. It has earned a reputation as a quality tablet for people who want something small, comfortable, and portable, but its small screen and comparatively limited processing power have restricted its appeal, making it best suited to watching media or playing games. With the 2026 version , the iPad mini is more competitive than ever. Its chip is current, its speakers are better, and, most impressively, it trades its 8.3-inch IPS screen for an 8.5-inch OLED that can hold its own against other premium tablets. There isn’t much more you can ask of an iPad this small. But at just $50 less than the larger, more powerful iPad Air (11-inch) , the iPad mini still has a hard time making a case for itself. title: Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe first drive: Where tech and fun collide
abstract: Mercedes-Benz provided flights from San Francisco to Malaga, Spain, and accommodation so Ars could drive the AMG GT 4-Door Coupe. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. The night before I drove the AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, I complained to a group of journalists that automakers don't want to take chances and just build fun, weird cars anymore. About 12 hours later, Mercedes made me eat my words. Outside of all the bombastic extravaganza of the Los Angeles launch, the first true AMG powered exclusively by batteries is a technological triumph that's as comfortable on the track as it is on the street. And it's really very good on the track. Triforce One of the fundamental problems with EVs is weight. Batteries are heavy, and the old rule about an object in motion tending to stay in motion makes the notion of nimble cornering a difficult engineering problem. Mercedes loves an engineering problem, and after two days behind the wheel of the AMG GT EV, the company has mostly reduced the battery-weight tax that mires EV performance. On the road and on the track, the vehicle is firmly planted to the roadway. Mercedes says various technologies make this possible. In addition to decades of producing high-performance vehicles, the automaker's AMG.EA sports-car architecture does a lot of heavy lifting here, constantly adjusting power delivery from the three motors while guiding the Active Ride Control suspension, steering—including up to 6 degrees at the rear axle—and active aerodynamics to deliver the performance AMG customers have come to expect from a vehicle with the Affalterbach badge on the hood. Read full article Comments

title: Nintendo's biggest ROM chip supplier is bowing out of the business
abstract: For years, the AI industry's insatiable demand for memory and storage has had plenty of knock-on effects on the price and availability of PC components like RAM , SSDs , and GPUs . Now those shortages are also squeezing the supply of ROM chips that power physical Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges. Chip manufacturer Macronix announced in its third-quarter earnings report that the company's production of ROM chips "has reached its end" and that it will begin "gradually decoupling from the game industry," as reported by Taiwanese news site BigGo Finance . That could be an issue for Nintendo, which, analyst David Gibson notes, uses Macronix as its "main memory chip maker" for physical game cartridges. That ROM production—which has shrunk 39 percent in the last year and now represents just 5 percent of Macronix's business—is being crowded out by production of more lucrative in-demand chips like NOR- and NAND-based memory and eMMCs, the company said. With Macronix's production capacity stuck at 25,000 12-inch wafers a month—and $1.2 billion in planned new capacity taking a year or more to spin up—less profitable ROM chips are taking up wafer space that can earn more through other types of chips. Read full article Comments

title: Hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones
abstract: Hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin exploited previously patched iOS and Android flaws in an attempt to hack visitors of multiple websites, including one celebrating the 250th anniversary of American independence, researchers said Wednesday. The attackers, which the researchers assessed with “moderate to high confidence” were part of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service, targeted other sites, many with links to that country’s ongoing war against Ukraine. The attacks began when iPhone or Android users visited one of potentially hundreds of different sites. JavaScript injected into the traffic then profiled the device. The final payloads, tailored to the type of platform visiting, attempted to steal browser cookies and, in some cases, Wi-Fi passwords and full mobile device data. Wielding DarkSword One of the impersonated sites was america250.org, belonging to a non-partisan group of lawmakers, business executives, and at least one former member of the Trump administration. The attackers registered america250[.]holiday and used it as a reverse proxy to america250.org. The imposter website delivered content from the real one but added malicious JavaScript into it. title: Uranium cubes reveal why the German nuclear project failed
abstract: During World War II, physicists on the Manhattan Project worried that the Nazi German nuclear program might achieve the first nuclear bomb before the US and its allies. That's not what transpired, but historians have debated just how close the Germans came to achieving criticality in their last attempt at building a reactor: the B8 pile. Werner Heisenberg, who led that effort, claimed that they were close and had only needed a little more uranium. But according to a paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences Nexus, that was not the case: The project simply didn't have sufficient uranium and heavy water to build a working bomb, given the design they were using. This particular research started in 2013, when University of Maryland physicist Timothy Koeth—a co-author on the new paper—received the gift of a mysterious heavy metal cube from a friend. He instantly recognized it as one of the uranium cubes used by German scientists in their unsuccessful attempt to build a working nuclear reactor. Only 14 such cubes are known to exist today. In 2019, we reported on Koeth’s quest to track down the cube’s origins, as well as several other similar cubes that had somehow found their way across the Atlantic. At the time, Koeth and his partner in the quest, then-graduate student Miriam “Mimi” Hiebert, had tracked down 10 such cubes around the US. For instance, the Smithsonian Institute had a German uranium cube in storage. They tracked a third cube to Harvard University, where it was regularly passed around to students in introductory physics classes as a curiosity. Read full article Comments

title: VMware releases vSphere Express for virtualization on up to 128 cores
abstract: After alienating many long-time small- to medium-sized business (SMB) customers, Broadcom’s VMware is trying to appeal to its smaller customers. Today, the virtualization company announced vSphere Express, a lower-end virtualization offering for organizations that require “cost-effective essential virtualization.” vSphere Express comes after many customers reported that VMware was pushing them to VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF), the flagship private cloud bundle that has many features SMBs don’t need and is expensive. Some SMB users have reported that VMware sales representatives previously told them that vSphere Standard, VMware's prior entry-level virtualization offering, wasn’t available anymore. abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ worklog-system 주간보고 자동화 구축 경험기 NAVER D2 | worklog-system 주간보고 자동화 구축 경험기 naver.me 발표 내용 대 AI 시대에 본인의 업무 기록을 수집하고 TODO 및 회의록을 기록하는 시스템을 소개합니다. ​ 이 도구를 만들며 부딪힌 세 가지 문제를 차례로 다룹니다. 기억이 아니라 기록에서 주간보고를 모으는 방법 재택과 사무실을 오가며 여러 기기와 VPN 환경에서 기록을 빠짐없이 모으는 구조 주간보고 화면에 노트·TODO·일정을 더해 업무 도구로 키우면서 중앙 서버 없이 해결한 과정 ​ <참고> 영상속 사내용어 OSS = 네이버 사내 GitHub Enterprise 인스턴스 ​ 발표 대상 주간보고를 쓰는 모든 직군 반복되는 업무 기록과 보고를 자동화하고 싶은 분 AI 도구와 사내 협업 도구(Slack, Jira, Confluence, GitHub)를 엮어 개인 생산성 도구를 만들어 보고 싶은 분 ​ 목차 데모: 하루 끝, 주간보고 끝 Episode 1. 주간보고 수집의 불편과 누락 Episode 2. 재택과 사무실 Episode 3. 업무 도구 하나로 지금의 형태와 앞으로 ​ ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

title: 2026년과 이후 JavaScript의 동향 - WebAssembly
abstract: 2020년 글 은 W3C 권고(1.0) 직후의 WebAssembly(이하 'wasm')를 다뤘습니다. '미래 버전에 포함될 작업'으로 스레드, SIMD(single instruction, multiple data), 참조 타입, 꼬리 호출, ESM(ECMAScript modules) 통합을 소개했고, Bytecode Alliance와 WASI(WebAssembly System Interface)가 그리는 브라우저 밖의 그림을 살펴봤습니다. 그리고 "아직까지 실서비스에서의 활발한 사용이 눈에 띄지는 않는다"라는 말과 함께, Sass가 wasm으로 플랫폼별 빌드 문제를 풀 수 있을지 모른다는 기대로 글을 맺었습니다. 이번 연재는 다음 네 편으로 구성됩니다. 1편: JavaScript(ECMAScript) 2편: 브라우저 밖의 JavaScript 3편: WebAssembly 4편: 라이브러리와 프레임워크 이 글에서는 2020년 글 이후 6년을 이어서 정리합니다. 2020년에 예고했던 기능들의 결말, wasm 2.0과 3.0, 지금 진행 중인 제안, WasmGC 덕분에 웹에서 쓸 수 있게 된 언어들, Component Model과 WASI가 바꾼 브라우저 밖의 생태계, JavaScript 개발자가 알게 모르게 쓰고 있는 wasm 패키지들을 살펴봅니다. 마지막으로 AI 도구와 에이전트가 wasm의 쓰임새를 어떻게 바꾸고 있는지도 정리합니다. 이 글의 내용은 2026년 10월을 기준으로 작성되었습니다. 글을 읽는 시점에 따라 글의 내용과 사실이 다를 수 있습니다. 2020년 이후 6년 2020년 글을 쓸 당시 wasm은 숫자 타입 네 가지( i32 , i64 , f32 , f64 )와 연속된 바이트 배열인 선형 메모리(linear memory)만 가진, 말 그대로 '컴파일 타깃'이었습니다. JavaScript와 문자열 하나를 주고받으려 해도 메모리에 바이트를 쓰고 그 위치를 숫자로 넘기는 글루 코드(glue code)가 필요했습니다. 6년이 지난 지금 wasm은 GC(가비지 컬렉션), 예외 처리, 64비트 주소 공간, 꼬리 호출을 명세에 담은 3.0이 되었습니다. Java, Kotlin, Dart 같은 GC 언어가 자체 런타임을 통째로 싣지 않고 wasm으로 컴파일됩니다. 브라우저 밖에서는 WASI가 Component Model 위로 옮겨 가며 0.2, 0.3이 나왔고, CDN 업체들이 wasm 기반 엣지 플랫폼을 운영하고 있습니다. 표 1 2019년 이후 주요 사건 시기 사건 2019년 12월 wasm 1.0 W3C 권고 2020년 10월 LibSass, Node Sass 비권장(deprecated) 지정 2023년 11월 V8 팀, WasmGC 포팅 가이드 공개(Chrome 119부터 WasmGC 지원) 2024년 1월 WASI 0.2 출시, WASI가 Component Model 기반으로 전환 2024년 6월 Google Sheets 계산 엔진의 WasmGC 전환 사례 공개 2024년 7월 Node Sass 지원 종료(end-of-life) 2024년 12월 W3C, wasm 2.0 후보 권고안 스냅샷 구현 요청 2025년 9월 wasm 3.0 발표 2025년 12월 Akamai, Fermyon 인수 발표 2026년 6월 WASI 0.3 출시, Safari 27 베타에서 JSPI(JS Promise Integration) 지원 Bytecode Alliance가 2026년 1월 발행한 10주년 회고 에 따르면, wasm은 2015년 6월 17일 4개 브라우저 벤더가 동시에 발표했고 2017년 말에 4대 브라우저가 모두 지원했습니다. 2019년 3월에 WASI가 발표되었고, 2024년 1월 WASI 0.2가 Component Model과 함께 나왔습니다. 2020년 '미래 버전에 포함될 작업'의 결말 2020년 글은 WebAssembly WG(Working Group)와 CG(Community Group)가 진행하던 작업으로 다섯 가지를 꼽았습니다. 6년이 지난 지금 다섯 항목 가운데 네 가지는 모든 주요 브라우저가 지원하지만, 명세상의 위치는 제각각입니다. 표 2 2020년에 소개한 기능의 현재 상태(2026년 10월 기준) 기능 명세상 위치 Chrome Firefox Safari 스레드 별도 제안(Phase 4) 74 79 14.1 128비트 SIMD wasm 2.0 91 89 16.4 참조 타입 wasm 2.0 96 79 15 꼬리 호출 wasm 3.0 112 121 18.2 ESM 통합 제안(Phase 3) 미지원 미지원 미지원 표 2의 브라우저 버전은 WebAssembly Feature Status 를, 제안의 단계는 WebAssembly/proposals 를 따랐습니다. 스레드 2020년 글은 Chrome 74부터 wasm 스레드가 기본 활성 상태라고 소개했습니다. 지금은 Firefox 79, Safari 14.1까지 지원 범위가 넓어졌습니다. 공유 메모리( SharedArrayBuffer )의 원자적 읽기와 쓰기, wait / notify 명령어로 구성된 이 제안 은 Phase 4(표준화 단계)에 있으며, 핵심 명세에는 아직 병합되지 않았습니다. 이 제안은 스레드 생성을 Web Workers에 맡기고, Emscripten 같은 툴체인이 이를 import로 노출하는 방식을 택했습니다. 공유 대상으로 정의한 것도 선형 메모리뿐이어서, 테이블, 전역 변수, WasmGC 객체는 스레드 사이에 공유할 수 없습니다. 이 한계를 다루는 후속 제안이 뒤에서 설명할 Shared-Everything Threads입니다. 128비트 SIMD 2020년 글에서 배열 4개 요소의 덧셈을 한 번의 CPU 명령으로 줄이는 예로 소개한 SIMD는 wasm 2.0에 Vector Instructions라는 이름으로 포함되었습니다. Chrome 91, Firefox 89, Safari 16.4부터 지원합니다(참고: Change History , WebAssembly Feature Status ). wasm 3.0에는 SIMD를 확장한 relaxed SIMD 가 추가되었습니다. 플랫폼별로 결과가 조금씩 다를 수 있는 연산(예: 융합 곱셈 덧셈)을 명세가 허용한 범위 안에서 하드웨어에 맞게 실행하도록 해 성능을 더 끌어냅니다. Chrome 114, Firefox 145에서 지원하고 Safari는 아직 플래그 뒤에 있습니다(참고: WebAssembly Feature Status ). 참조 타입 wasm 코드가 호스트 객체를 직접 참조하게 하는 참조 타입(reference types)은 wasm 2.0에 포함되었습니다. funcref 와 externref 두 가지 값 타입이 추가되었고, externref 로 JavaScript 객체를 wasm 쪽에서 숫자 인덱스로 바꾸지 않고 그대로 들고 있을 수 있게 되었습니다(참고: Change History ). 참조 타입은 이후 wasm 3.0의 typed function references와 GC의 바탕이 되었습니다. 꼬리 호출 추가 스택 공간을 쓰지 않고 함수를 호출하는 꼬리 호출(tail calls)은 wasm 3.0에 return_call , return_call_indirect 명령어로 포함되었습니다. 함수형 언어(Scheme, OCaml 등)의 컴파일러가 재귀를 반복문으로 바꾸는 우회 기법 없이 wasm을 생성할 수 있게 되었습니다(참고: Change History ). V8은 v11.2에서 꼬리 호출을 출시 했고, Emscripten으로 C++ 코루틴을 구현하는 사례를 함께 소개했습니다. 그림 1 꼬리 호출 시 호출자 프레임을 정리한 뒤 피호출 함수를 실행하는 스택 변화(출처: WebAssembly tail calls ) ESM 통합 다섯 항목 가운데 유일하게 아직 브라우저에 기본 탑재되지 않은 기능입니다. 제안은 Phase 3(구현 단계)에 있고, JavaScript 쪽 문법인 TC39의 Source Phase Imports도 Stage 3입니다(참고: WebAssembly/proposals , TC39 proposals ). 진행 상황은 뒤의 ' 진행 중인 제안 ' 절에서 자세히 설명합니다. wasm 2

title: 크림에서 통합 임베딩(Universal Embedding)은 어떻게 쓰일까?
abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ 크림에서 통합 임베딩(Universal Embedding)은 어떻게 쓰일까? NAVER D2 | 크림에서 통합 임베딩(Universal Embedding)은 어떻게 쓰일까? naver.me ​ 발표 내용 여러 엔티티를 한 공간에 담은 통합 임베딩과 범용 리트리벌이 크림 추천 곳곳에 쓰이는 방식, 운영하며 드러난 한계를 v2에서 해결한 과정, 그리고 확장 방향을 공유합니다. ​ 발표 대상 추천 시스템의 후보 생성(Retrieval) 단계에 관심 있으신 분들 여러 서비스·지면에서 함께 쓰는 공용 임베딩을 설계하고 운영하고 싶으신 ML 엔지니어 조건(필터)이 걸린 벡터 검색의 지연과 메모리를 줄이고 싶으신 분들 구좌·서비스마다 늘어나는 추천 모델을 줄이고 싶은 추천·검색 조직의 엔지니어와 기획자 ​ 키워드 Recommendation System / Candidate Generation (Retrieval) Universal Embedding (Bi-encoder · Contrastive Learning) Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) Filtered Vector Retrieval (Roaring Bitmap · Brute-force vs ANN) Embedding Serving Optimization ​ 목차 PART 1. 왜 통합 임베딩인가 2025년의 크림: 추천 구좌마다 모델이 따로 있었다 목표: 여러 목적에 쓸 수 있는 범용 임베딩 하나 구좌마다 ‘누구에게 · 무엇을 · 어떻게’가 다르다 통합 임베딩은 후보 생성에 직접, 랭킹에도 입력으로 설계 원칙: 모든 질문이 ‘벡터 + 조건’이 된다 PART 2. v1 모델 — 하나의 공간을 만들다 하나의 인코더가 검색어와 상품을 모두 읽는다 학습: InfoNCE를 받쳐 주는 일곱 가지 장치 학습은 상품 하나, 나머지는 모두 집계로 그림으로 보면: 모두가 상품 공간 위의 점 PART 3. v1 리트리벌 — 하나의 API로 꺼내 쓰다 질문 하나 = 요청 하나 조건별 상품 목록을 미리 만들어 두고 꺼내 쓰기 구좌 전용 모델 없이 붙은 첫 구좌들과 타겟 집단 추천 PART 4. 써 보니 드러난 v1의 한계 모델: 가끔 붕괴하고, 768차원은 무거웠다 리트리벌: 큰 조건을 감당하지 못했다 리트리벌: 조건을 자유롭게 조합할 수 없었다 v1의 한계, 한눈에 PART 5. v2 — 한계를 하나씩 걷어내다 모델 1차: 학습을 안정시키다 모델 2차: 하나의 벡터, 여러 해상도 (MRL) 좌표계: 회전으로 맞추려 했지만, 통하지 않았다 필터: Roaring Bitmap으로 조건을 실행할 때 조합 왜 근사 검색(ANN)이 아니라 후보 전부를 계산하나 점수 계산: 계산량은 그대로, 메모리 낭비만 없앴다 결과: 응답 지연은 약 4배 빠르게, 메모리는 1/6로 API: 조건 칸 하나 → 조건 리스트 v1의 한계 → v2의 처방 PART 6. 지금의 쓰임과 다음 확장 지금: 하나의 API가 채우는 지면과 구좌 비슷한 브랜드: 브랜드 벡터만으로는 부족했다 리트리벌 밖에서도 같은 벡터 다음으로 — 멀티벡터, 지면 확장, 마케팅 타겟팅 ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

title: FE News 26년 11월 소식을 전해드립니다.
abstract: 주요소식 26년 11월 소식에서는 다음과 같은 유용한 정보들을 만나보실 수 있습니다. ​ Tailwind Labs is joining Shopify Tailwind CSS를 만든 Adam Wathan이 Tailwind Labs의 Shopify 합류를 발표했다. Tailwind CSS를 비롯한 오픈소스 프로젝트는 계속 MIT 라이선스로 남고 Tailwind 팀이 Shopify의 지원을 받아 유지보수를 이어 가므로, 이미 쓰고 있는 팀이 당장 바꿀 것은 없다. 대신 유료 컴포넌트·템플릿 모음 Tailwind Plus와 에이전트 스킬 모음 ui.sh는 신규 가입을 받지 않으며, Wathan은 사용자와 같은 문제를 겪는 실제 커머스 제품 안에서 프레임워크를 개발하고 싶었다고 배경을 설명한다. ​ ​ ​ Introducing tsrs: a Port of TypeScript to Rust Cloudflare와 VoidZero가 TypeScript 컴파일러를 Rust로 옮기는 tsrs를 Oxc 툴체인 안에서 개발한다고 발표했다. Go로 다시 작성한 TypeScript 7보다 WebAssembly 환경에 잘 맞고 메모리를 적게 쓰는 것이 목표로, 팀의 초기 벤치마크에서는 TypeScript 7.0보다 최대 8배 빠르고 메모리를 약 70% 덜 썼다. 비슷한 시기에 나온 ts-rust, Bun의 bun check, Vercel Labs의 tsc-ts도 함께 소개하며, 모두 실험 단계이므로 CI 타입 검사가 병목인 팀이라면 기존 tsc와 진단 결과를 비교하며 시험해 볼 만하다. ​ ​ ​ Making React Context Cheap with React Compiler Context 값이 바뀌면 그 Context를 읽는 모든 컴포넌트가 다시 렌더링되는 비용을 React Compiler로 줄이는 방법을 다룬 글이다. 라디오 버튼 5,000개 예제에서 컴포넌트를 나누지 않고 Context를 그대로 읽게 둔 채 메모이제이션을 React Compiler에 맡기면, 클릭 처리 시간이 useSyncExternalStore 스토어나 React.memo로 나눈 방식과 비슷한 수준이 된다. 저자는 렌더링 횟수보다 렌더링 한 번의 작업량이 사용자 체감을 좌우한다며, 렌더링을 없애기보다 싸게 만드는 데 집중하라고 권한다. ​ ​ ​ React 19.3 실험 단계였던 <ViewTransition>과 Fragment Refs가 안정화되었다. <ViewTransition>은 Transition으로 표시된 업데이트에서 요소의 등장, 퇴장, 갱신에 View Transition API 애니메이션을 적용하고, Fragment Refs로는 래퍼 요소 없이 형제 DOM 노드 묶음에 이벤트 리스너나 Observer를 연결할 수 있다. 컴포넌트를 서버 렌더링에서 제외하는 browser() API와 Trusted Types 지원도 추가되었으며, Strict Mode가 하이드레이션 중에도 Effect를 두 번 실행하므로 업그레이드 후에는 정리 함수가 없는 Effect부터 점검해 둬야 한다. ​ ​ ​ Remix 3 Remix 3이 Remix Jam 2026에 맞춰 첫 안정 버전으로 출시되었다. remix 패키지 하나에 라우터, 데이터베이스 관리, 스키마 검증, 에셋 서버, React가 아닌 자체 UI 런타임을 담은 풀스택 프레임워크이며, 기존 Remix 2 앱은 Remix 3이 아니라 React Router로 옮기게 된다. 10월 23일 나온 3.1은 코드 변경 없이 서버 렌더링을 약 두 배 빠르게 했고, 팀은 정식 출시 이후 SemVer를 지키겠다고 밝혔다. ​ ​ ​ >> FE News 26년 11월 소식 보러가기 ◎ FE News란? 네이버 FE 엔지니어들이 엄선한 양질의 FE 및 주요한 기술 소식들을 큐레이션해 공유하는 것을 목표로 하며, 이를 통해 국내 개발자들에게 지식 공유에 대한 가치 인식과 성장에 도움을 주고자 하는 기술소식 공유 프로젝트 입니다. 매월 첫째 주 수요일, 월 1회 발행 되고 있으니 많은 관심 부탁드립니다. ▷ 구독하기

title: 딸깍으로 안되는 Multi-interest 개발기
abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ 딸깍으로 안되는 Multi-interest 개발기 NAVER D2 | 딸깍으로 안되는 Multi-interest 개발기 naver.me ​ 발표 내용 다양한 관심사 추천 모델인 Multi-interest를 여러 지면에 적용하며 겪었던 문제를 해결했던 과정을 공유합니다. ​ 주제: Multi-interest 추천 모델(MINER)의 KREAM 실서비스 적용 사례 문제: 인기 상품 목록에서 특정 상품이 전체 유저에게 동시 노출되는 hubness 발생 분석: 점수를 유저 의존 성분과 유저 무관 성분으로 분해, 가설 3개를 실측으로 검증 조치: 유저 무관 성분 제거(centering, bias 분리), 추천 결과 다양화, 분포 지표 기반 평가 체계 도입 결과: 과노출 상품 전량 제거, 노출 상품 종류 +25%, 구매 지표 유지 시사점: 논문 구조의 실서비스 적용 시 발생하는 문제와 사전 점검 항목 ​ 발표 대상 Multi-interest 추천 모델에 관심 있으신 분들 ​ 목차 문제상황 가설 수립, 유저 의존 성분 + 유저 무관 성분 전략 1. 유저 무관 성분 낮추기 전략 2. 유저 유관 성분 높이기 전략 3. 두 성분을 지표에서 모니터링 남은 과제 및 점검항목 ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

title: AI 에이전트를 위한 멀티모달 의사결정 모델 ‘Kanana-2-v-decide’ 오픈소스 공개
abstract: 안녕하세요, 카카오 Applied AI Model팀의 Shawn(정성효), Michael(이주영)입니다. 고객 문의를 분류하고, 상품 사진을 확인하고, 에이전트가 다음 작업에 사용할 도구를 고르는 일. 서비스에는 긴 답변보다 명확한 판단이 필요한 순간이 많습니다. 특히 AI 에이전트는 하나의 요청을 처리하는 동안 이러한 판단을 여러 차례 반복합니다. Agentic AI 시대에 각 단계에서 필요한 판단 결과를 빠르게 얻고, 이를 서비스의 다음 동작으로 ...

title: 국내 최초 광고 MCP를 출시하며, 개발자의 역할은 어디까지 넓어졌을까?
abstract: 안녕하세요. 당근 광고실 광고주플랫폼팀에서 백엔드 엔지니어로 일하는 제이크(Jake)예요. 얼마 전 저희 팀 엔지니어링 매니저 Iltaek이 프론트엔드와 백엔드를 한 팀으로 합친 이야기 를 글로 나눴어요. 그 글이 팀의 경계를 넘어 일하는 이야기였다면, 이번 글은 제가 당근 광고 MCP를 만들며 개발자의 역할을 넓혀 본 이야기 예요. MCP(Model Context Protocol)는 AI 서비스가 외부 서비스의 데이터를 불러올 때 쓰는 표준 연결 방식이에요. 광고주가 Claude 같은 AI 서비스에 “지난주 광고 성과 어땠어?”라고 물으면, AI가 광고 MCP를 거쳐 당근 광고의 계정 정보와 광고 정보, 성과 데이터를 가져와서 답해 줘요. 해외 광고 플랫폼에서는 구글, 메타, 아마존이 이미 MCP를 공개했고, 국내에서는 당근이 처음으로 공식 광고 MCP를 출시했어요. 저는 개발자로 이 프로젝트에 참여하는 줄 알았는데, 하다 보니 로드맵과 PRD부터 출시까지 맡아야 했어요. 이 글에서는 그 과정에서 겪은 일과, 제가 일하는 방식이 어떻게 달라졌는지 이야기해 보려고 해요. 로드맵과 PRD를 처음 써 봤어요 그동안은 PM과 함께 일하면서 엔지니어로서 개발에 필요한 의견을 나누고, PRD를 어떻게 구현할지 고민했어요. 그런데 이번에는 Iltaek에게 로드맵과 PRD까지 맡아 달라는 요청을 받았어요. 솔직히 요청을 받았을 때는 “이것도 개발자인 내 일인가?” 싶었어요. 로드맵은 PM이 그리는 거 아닌가, 내가 로드맵을 제시하는 게 맞나 하는 생각이 먼저 들었어요. 해 본 적 없는 일이라 부담도 됐고요. 그때 Iltaek이 오너라는 마음가짐으로 해 보라고 했어요. 그 말대로 “내 프로젝트”라고 생각하다 보니, 이 프로젝트를 더 잘되게 하려면 뭘 해야 할지 고민하게 되더라고요. 스스로 던지는 질문부터 달라졌어요. 로드맵을 그리려고 하니, 당근 광고 플랫폼은 생각보다 크고 복잡했어요. 전문가모드, 간편모드, 대행사 플랫폼¹까지 합치면 광고주가 할 수 있는 일이 정말 많아요. 광고 보고서, 광고 수정, 소재 만들기, 타겟팅, 전환 추적, 결제와 충전까지요. 이걸 한 번에 다 MCP로 열 수는 없어서, 범위를 좁혀야 했어요. 혹시나 잘못되더라도 광고주에게 손해가 없는 일인지, 화면보다 AI로 했을 때 더 편한 일인지, 더 많은 광고주에게 도움이 되는 일인지, 이렇게 세 가지 기준을 세워 봤어요. 그래서 리스크가 가장 낮은 조회 기능부터 열었어요. 광고를 수정하는 기능은 충분히 검증한 뒤에 열기로 했어요. AI가 예산이나 입찰가를 바꾸다 실수하면 광고비가 의도와 다르게 나갈 수 있어서요. 결제나 광고 삭제처럼 AI로 하는 게 오히려 불편하거나 위험한 일은 아예 열지 않기로 했어요. 그리고 당근 광고에서 가장 많이 집행되는 디스플레이 광고부터 시작했어요. 그렇게 로드맵을 그리고, 그 안에서 이번에 할 일의 범위를 정했어요. 그다음 저희 팀에서 쓰는 PTBSMAF라는 프레임워크로 PRD를 썼어요. 문제 정의(Problem Statement), 트레이드오프(Trade-off), 벤치마크(Benchmark), 해결책(Solution), 지표(Metrics), 중단 조건(Andon), 피드백 루프(Feedback Loop)의 앞 글자를 딴 이름이에요. 그중에서도 문제 정의, 트레이드오프, 벤치마크가 특히 도움이 됐어요. 문제를 제가 이해한 대로 풀어 쓰다 보니 생각이 정리됐고, 조회만 먼저 열면 무엇을 얻고 무엇을 포기하는지 적으면서 트레이드오프가 분명해졌어요. 특히 벤치마크에서는 다른 광고 플랫폼의 사례를 찾아보면서, 그대로 참고할 부분과 우리 상황에 맞게 바꿔야 할 부분이 구분됐어요. PRD를 쓰면서 이전에는 생각해 보지 못했던 부분까지 고민하게 됐어요. 이 기능으로 플랫폼이 무엇을 얻을지, 어느 제품부터 고려할지, 뭐가 더 나은 방향인지 같은 제품 관점의 고민은 전부 처음이었어요. 이렇게 정한 것들이 정답인지 100% 확신할 수는 없었지만, 적어도 근거를 가지고 정했다는 점은 지금 돌아봐도 만족스러워요. 로드맵은 PM이 그리는 거라고 생각했던 것도, 해 보고 나니 제 선입견이었던 것 같아요. API를 그대로 옮기면 될 줄 알았어요 로드맵과 PRD로 무엇을 하고 무엇을 하지 않을지 정하고 나니, 이제 도구를 어떻게 만들지 고민할 차례였어요. 광고주센터 뒤에는 이미 잘 돌아가는 API가 있어서, 그걸 MCP 도구로 하나씩 감싸기만 하면 될 거라고 생각했어요. 그런데 API를 그대로 도구로 만들면, AI가 어떤 도구를 써야 할지 헷갈려하고, 필요한 정보를 놓쳐 잘못된 답을 할 수 있더라고요. 예를 들어 광고주가 “이 광고 왜 안 나가?”라고 물었다고 해 볼게요. 광고주센터였다면 광고 정보, 노출 상태, 심사 결과가 한 화면에 같이 보였을 거예요. 그런데 API마다 도구를 따로 만들면, AI가 그중 뭘 부를지 스스로 골라야 해요. 광고 정보만 보고 “켜져 있으니 괜찮아요”라고 답하면서, 광고 심사에서 막힌 건 놓치는 식이에요. 메타 광고 MCP를 직접 연결해 보니, 도구가 많고 설명 방식도 제각각이라 AI가 광고주의 요청을 다르게 이해하는 경우가 있었어요. 로드맵을 그리며 광고주가 AI에게 무엇을 물어볼지 고민했던 게 여기서 도움이 됐어요. API를 그대로 옮기는 대신, 광고주의 질문을 기준으로 도구를 설계하기로 했어요. 그렇게 정리해 보니 좋은 API와 좋은 도구의 기준은 꽤 달랐어요. 이 기준으로, 가장 흔한 요청인 “지난주 성과 분석해 줘”를 예시로 도구를 설계해 봤어요. 이 요청은 어느 계정인지 정하고, 대상을 찾고, 성과를 보는 세 단계로 나눌 수 있어요. 그래서 단계마다 도구를 하나씩 두고 광고주센터 뒤의 여러 API를 3개의 도구로 정리했어요. 앞으로 광고 수정처럼 기능이 늘어나면 도구도 함께 늘어나겠지만, 그때도 이 기준을 지켜 가려고 해요. 제품으로 내놓으려면 챙길 게 많았어요 도구를 다 만들었다고 바로 내놓을 수 있는 건 아니었어요. AI가 광고주의 계정을 대신 다룰 수 있도록 약관을 검토하고 법무팀의 확인을 받아야 했어요. 기존 서버에 부하가 가지 않도록 적절한 호출 한도를 정해야 했고, 광고주용 연결 가이드와 서비스 내 안내 화면도 준비해야 했어요. 그리고 출시 후 운영을 위한 대시보드도 만들어야 했어요. 처음에는 좀 막막했어요. 일정을 챙기고, 회의를 잡고, 다른 팀과 일정을 맞추는 일은 개발자인 저에게 익숙하지 않았으니까요. 그럴 때마다 함께 진행한 PM인 Moana와 이야기하면서 하나씩 풀어 나갔어요. 챙길 일 중에서도 가장 걱정했던 건 인증 이었어요. MCP는 인증 방식이 표준으로 정해져 있어요. OAuth 2.1을 따라야 하고, MCP를 연결할 때 광고주 본인의 동의를 거쳐야 해요. 사내에서만 쓰는 게 아니라 외부 광고주에게 공개하려면, 이러한 표준을 반드시 지원해야 했어요. 다행히 당근의 인증을 맡고 있는 Identity Service Team에서 이미 SSO(Single Sign-On)를 제공하고 있었어요.² 그래서 MCP 인증도 지원해 달라고 요청드렸고, 인증 서버를 표준에 맞게 고쳐 주셨어요. 그리고 나서 광고 MCP에 인증 서버를 연동하고 AI 서비스에 연결해 봤어요. 그런데 OpenAI의 Codex에서는 로그인을 누르면 에러가 뜨고 그대로 끊겼어요. OpenAI 문서에는 이 표준을 지원한다고 나와 있어서 더 당황했는데, 알고 보니 그때 이 인증 방식에 대한 지원은 Codex 정식 버전에는 아직 들어가지 않았고 알파 버전에만 막 들어온 참이었어요. 이대로 출시하면 Codex에서는 광고 MCP를 연결할 수 없는 상황이었어요. 그래서 틈날 때마다 새 버전이 나왔는지 들여다봤어요. 출시 전에 정식 버전에서도 지원하게 돼서, 그제야 한숨 돌렸어요. 그렇게 9월 16일, 광고 MCP를 공개 베타로 출시했어요. 출시 후엔 광고주가 어떻게 쓰는지 궁금했어요 원래라면 개발하고 QA하고 프로덕션에 배포하면 끝났다고 생각했을 것 같아요. 그런데 제품을 맡고 보니, 배포하고 나서 의도한 대로 동작하는지가 궁금했어요. 광고주들이 이걸 실제로 어떻게 쓰는지, 어떻게 하면 더 잘 쓰게 할 수 있을지 계속 고민하게 됐어요. 그래서 도구가

title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
abstract: Researchers use large language models as agents in social simulations, where agents are prompted with observations and background information intended to shape their actions. Yet LLM agents have been shown to substantially change their behavior under meaning-preserving prompt variations, creating a validation problem for social simulation. One plausible hypothesis is that this brittleness reflects a lack of grounding and can be reduced by enriching the context provided to the agents. Whether richer context improves robustness remains unclear, in part because context richness and robustness are rarely defined in ways that support controlled comparisons. We address the first need with controlled context enrichment, a set of prompt substitution rules that systematically enriches distinct types of context: neutral padding, generic social background, descriptive decision grounding, and normative decision grounding. We address the second by introducing selective robustness as a validation criterion: insensitivity to meaning-preserving prompt variation combined with a directional response to decision-relevant changes in the social world. We demonstrate the framework in a Prisoner's Dilemma-like game, showing how it can be used to identify which forms of context enrichment produce more desirable and robust agent behavior. We find that these forms of enrichment produce distinct behavioral patterns that vary between the two models tested.

title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories
abstract: Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories (SDCLs) are moving chemical experimentation toward embodied automation, where machines must perceive laboratory scenes, reason about experimental states, and act under physical, procedural, and safety constraints. Although Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly considered as embodied brains for such systems, existing laboratory benchmarks mainly focus on safety, anomaly detection, or general scientific understanding, leaving their execution-oriented embodied capabilities underexplored. To fill this gap, we introduce BEAKER, a Benchmark for evaluating Embodied Actionability, Knowledge, Experimentation, and Reasoning in SDCLs. BEAKER contains 1,000 expert-curated question-answer samples across 11 image and video task types, covering key judgments required for chemical laboratory execution, including affordance grounding, trajectory planning, equipment, state, and safety recognition, apparatus setup, operation and step reasoning, and temporal procedure reasoning. All questions and annotations are manually created and reviewed by chemistry and embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) experts, without AI-assisted generation or annotation. We evaluate 28 general-purpose, science-oriented, chemistry-specialized, and embodied MLLMs in an offline, single-turn setting. Results show that current models can follow coarse experimental procedures in videos, but still struggle to ground actions into operable regions and feasible trajectories, to recognize fine-grained laboratory apparatus, states, and safety norms, and to order steps in mid-length procedures. BEAKER thus reveals a clear gap between coarse procedural understanding and the precise, action-grounded perception required for laboratory execution, providing a diagnostic benchmark for future MLLMs in SDCLs.

title: Occlusion for Free: Detecting Occlusion from the Disagreement Between Two Monocular Distance Cues
abstract: Knowing that a pedestrian is occluded is useful to a robot even when the detector cannot recover the hidden pixels, but occlusion estimators are normally trained on occlusion annotations that deployment settings rarely have. We show that occlusion can be read off two distance estimates a camera-only pipeline already computes. Apparent height is largely unchanged by occlusion, because the detected box still spans the whole person; monocular metric depth is pulled toward the occluder, because the nearest surface inside the box is what a depth map reports. Only their ordering matters, so no focal length, stature, or depth scale is needed, provided the depth model's error is close to a pure gain, a condition that can be checked without labels. The score detects heavy occlusion on KITTI with AUC 0.909 (0.888 over all annotated pedestrians, including those the detector misses), requires no training and no occlusion labels, and is not a proxy for range: within fixed distance bands it holds AUC 0.894-0.925 while true distance alone sits near chance. On synthetic CARLA scenes with measured visibility it reaches 0.819, against 0.644 for distance alone. We arrived here after measuring three standard architectural responses to occlusion, depth fusion, occlusion-simulating augmentation, and attention, none of which improved detection outside its training distribution in the configurations we tested, and after finding that a detector trained on German roads loses half its accuracy on self-annotated street scenes in Lagos, Nigeria. Signals that need no local annotation are worth more in settings that benchmarks do not represent.

title: Energy-Guided Transport for Projection-Free Physics-Informed Flow Matching
abstract: Deep generative models, particularly Flow Matching frameworks, have emerged as powerful tools for synthesizing complex physical systems. However, standard architectures remain purely statistically driven and agnostic to the underlying governing equations, often violating fundamental physical constraints during inference. Existing zero-shot approaches designed to enforce these constraints typically rely on rigid algebraic projections. While effective for sparse boundary conditions, applying such discrete geometric corrections to dense, full-domain PDEs may disrupt the probability path, \rev{potentially deviating from the learned manifold and introducing substantial computational overhead}. To address these challenges, we introduce Energy-Guided Transport, a novel training-free framework that formulates non-linear physical constraints as a smooth potential energy landscape. Rather than interrupting the ODE integration, our method applies a continuous dissipative force directly to the intermediate generative states, steering them toward the physical manifold. By evaluating this force implicitly via reverse-mode automatic differentiation, our framework preserves the natural dynamics of the flow while maintaining an efficient $\mathcal{O}(N)$ algorithmic complexity. We extensively evaluate our framework across various 1D and 2D physical systems, including the chaotic Navier-Stokes equations. Our method achieves stable generation without structural divergence, significantly improves the stability-accuracy trade-off compared to state-of-the-art methods, and substantially accelerates inference with respect to exact projection strategies. Code available at: https://github.com/ispamm/Projection-free-energy-guided-flow-matching.

title: From Admission to Retention: Predicting Durable Offspring in Quality-Diversity Search
abstract: Automated failure discovery can be framed as a diversity problem: the objective is to expose distinct ways a system fails rather than a single critical adversarial case. Yet uniform parent sampling provides no way to allocate search effort toward individuals likely to produce durable archive contributions. We study this credit assignment problem in an unstructured Quality-Diversity (QD) archive, testing whether signals available before an individual has reproduced distinguish offspring that merely enter the archive from those still retained generations later. Across a planar-arm benchmark and two robotic-locomotion tasks, the same signals are often associated with entry and persistence in opposite directions. In particular, lineage depth is the clearest such signal, and its persistence discrimination grows with population capacity, which is associated with lower turnover. Biasing parent selection toward the signals with the strongest measured association to survival nevertheless does not improve search: moderate bias matches uniform sampling, and strong bias reduces QD-score.

title: Nowcasting Future Performance for Population Pruning in Survival-of-the-Fittest Training
abstract: Training high-performing neural networks often involves evaluating populations of candidate models with varying hyperparameters, architectures, or random seeds. Training every candidate to completion is computationally expensive, yet stopping seemingly weaker runs early risks discarding models that would ultimately perform better, as learning curves can cross. To address this challenge, we investigate whether intermediate training checkpoints can predict future model accuracy and enable more informed pruning decisions. Our nowcasters predict test accuracy five epochs ahead or at the end of training. They are trained with accuracy and loss histories, weight statistics, and SANE representations as inputs. SANE is a transformer autoencoder that encodes a checkpoint as a sequence of latent tokens. We then use the nowcasters in Survival-of-the-Fittest (SOTF) training. SOTF repeatedly ranks runs during training by predicted accuracy and stops the lowest-ranked ones.
